Qwen3-MoE scaling ladder: KD vs CE

Document-isolated eval (9 decon suites incl. private_internal), dpl metric definitions; generated 2026-10-29 15:11

Findings

  • KD beats CE at every rung, on every validation set, for every α (all 135 cells negative).
  • The gain grows with scale: KD lowers overall_tw loss by 0.041 → 0.045 → 0.049 → 0.052 → 0.055 (q0 → q4).
  • Equivalent size: KD models match CE models with 1.19 → 1.25 → 1.31 → 1.43× the active parameters (interpolated on CE's loss vs log N curve), and the multiplier grows with scale.
  • The gain is largest on uncheatable / codefresh and smallest on val_v2 and private_internal; private_internal is a private set outside the training corpus, and KD improves it consistently too.
  • α 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 are indistinguishable (largest gap 0.004); the choice of α does not change the conclusion.
  • Optimizers (all CE): MuonH's overall_tw gain over AdamW shrinks with scale (0.079 → 0.039 → 0.026 → 0.019 → 0.013 (q0 → q4)), while KD's gain grows - the KD benefit holds up at scale better than the optimizer change.
  • KD loss variants (same α 0.8, MuonH): the sampled-tail variants beat B64 consistently, but the lead shrinks with scale (overall_tw, q0 → q2: S64Y -0.0059 → -0.0045 → -0.0029 → -0.0036; S64 -0.0023 → -0.0052 → -0.0035 → -0.0035; S128 -0.0023 → -0.0040 → -0.0031 → -0.0036); the bucket variants are ≈ 0 (B64Y -0.0002 → -0.0017 → +0.0007; B128 -0.0008 → -0.0018 → +0.0001).
  • MuonH learning rate (overall_tsqw, parabola-fitted best multiple m*, * = vertex outside the sampled multiples, extrapolated): q0@9.6B (TPP 200)1.23× (η* 0.0165); q0@28.8B (TPP 600)1.32× (η* 0.0125); q0@86.4B (TPP 1800)1.51× (η* 0.0100); q1@9.6B (TPP 62)1.48× (η* 0.0162); q1@30.8B (TPP 200)1.52× (η* 0.0114); q2@9.6B (TPP 27)1.62× (η* 0.0153); q2@30.8B (TPP 87)1.70× (η* 0.0111); q2@71.1B (TPP 200)1.73× (η* 0.0086); q3@9.6B (TPP 14)1.66× (η* 0.0141); q4@9.6B (TPP 8)1.76× (η* 0.0136); q5@9.6B (TPP 5)1.82× (η* 0.0131); q6@9.6B (TPP 3.5)1.80× (η* 0.0121); q3@30.8B (TPP 45)1.76× (η* 0.0103).

Router choice: softmax or DeepSeek-V3 style (MuonH / AdamW, fitted LR law, 128-choose-8, q0 three seeds)

Boxiang's controlled experiment of 10-26 (design: reports/dsv3_router_experiment_design_2026-10-26.md). The softmax + aux-loss router is replaced by the DeepSeek-V3 router (sigmoid scores + a per-expert bias for load balance + seq aux 1e-4); 128-choose-8 experts and everything else unchanged; the MuonH arms use the fitted LR law (MUONH_FIT), the AdamW arm BASE's own LR rule. Values = arm − partner (doc-isolated, negative = the arm is better); at q0 three seeds paired per seed, mean ± se (number of paired seeds in brackets); pre-registered lines: |Δ| < 0.003 = no difference, single seed ±0.008.

The two routers

softmax router (the original, control)

  • Softmax over the logits of the 128 experts; the 8 highest scores are picked.
  • Load balance by an aux loss (Switch style, coefficient 1e-3): when some experts are picked too often, an extra penalty pushes the router to spread the tokens.

DSV3 router (DeepSeek-V3 style)

  • Each expert score goes through its own sigmoid, each in 0-1, not competing with the others.
  • Experts are picked by “score + bias”. Every expert has a bias that is not a trained parameter but adjusted by a rule every step: an overloaded expert gets bias − 0.001, an underloaded one + 0.001.
  • The bias only decides which experts are picked, not their output weights: after the 8 are picked, their weights are their original sigmoid scores (without the bias), normalised over those 8 (Megatron moe_utils.py L953-959).
  • A small aux loss is kept as well (seq aux 1e-4), computed per sequence.
  • Design idea: balance mainly by the bias and hardly by an aux loss, so the aux loss does not interfere with the main task.
Which optimizer and LR for the gate (router weights)

The gate is the weight matrix Wg (128 × width) that computes the logits.

  • AdamH: the MuonH default - Adam updates, but the weights are kept on a sphere of fixed radius (hyperball); the weight norm cannot grow.
  • AdamW: plain AdamW; the weight norm is free (wd 0 in B2).
  • router LR ×1: the gate uses the same LR as the body (0.0164 at q0 under the fitted law).
  • router LR ×0.19: the gate LR is lowered to ~3.1e-3, about the AdamW baseline own LR level. The earlier probe B1 showed that an AdamW gate at ×1 saturates the logits, hence 0.19.

Health from the router monitor of Boxiang (DECISIONS 10-26 19:1x-19:2x): A at q1-q3 has expert bias 3-5 (pre-registered limit 1) and runaway logits 60-87, load balanced only by the bias - not adoptable as is under the pre-registered rule; B2 (AdamW gate) pins ~10 % of the selected experts' scores near 1, bias above 1, logits rising; B3 (AdamH gate, router LR ×0.19) and C are healthy. The two pathologies have different causes: at router LR ×1 the AdamH gate of A does not learn the balance itself and the bias keeps growing, which router LR ×0.19 (B3) fixes; B2 and B3 share the router LR and only B2, with the AdamW gate, pins the selected scores near 1, so the pinning comes from the AdamW gate itself (DECISIONS 10-26 17:29).

Router load-balancing loss: negative-entropy loss instead (MuonH, DeepSeek-V3-style router, fitted LR law; Runlong TODO 9)

Priority 1 of Runlong now (arXiv 2605.15403). The router load-balancing loss (DSV3 base: seq aux 1e-4; softmax base: Switch aux 1e-3) is replaced by the paper's negative-entropy balancing loss: per layer an EMA (η 0.65) of the router probabilities m, loss = α·E·Σ p_e·(log m_e + 1). The DSV3 base keeps its expert bias. Values = arm − pair (doc-isolated, negative = better), q0 seed 1 so far (single-seed line ±0.008; paired q0 seed scatter ~±0.001). Decision rule of Runlong at the q2 reading: three seeds + q1 + q2 same sign, |Δ| ≥ 0.003, ≥ 3 se, health no worse.

MuonH learning rate: the best LR in each cell (same MuonH, CE)

This section always uses overall_tsqw (token-sqrt-weighted: all 7 collections - val_v2, uncheatable, codefresh, v3small, private_internal, pile_test, pile_10k - each at its token-weighted loss, averaged with weights ∝ √(scored tokens); weights ≈ uncheatable 31 %, pile_test 23 %, val_v2 15 %, codefresh 13 %, pile_10k 8 %, private_internal 5 %, v3small 5 % - between tw and macro, so neither the longest nor the shortest collection dominates; unlike overall_tw / macro, pile_10k is included); it does not follow the metric toggle above. Each cell = one fixed (model size, training tokens). In a cell, one model per 0.5 / 0.7 / 1 / 1.2 / 1.4 / 2 (/ 2.8 / 4) × the HyperP-law LR; y = loss difference to the cell's 1× (lower is better); the big number = the fitted best multiple m* (the parabola vertex, possibly extrapolated beyond the sampled multiples; m* > 1 means the law is too low), below it the absolute LR η* (in parentheses the cell's 1× LR, i.e. the HyperP-law LR for its depth and training tokens) and how much the optimum beats 1×; the main-ladder TPP 200 cells run along the diagonal; hover a cell to see its LR sweep curve (dashed = parabola in log(multiple), orange = m*). Read a column for depth, the q0 row for training length. Cells have different budgets: compare only within a cell. Blank = not in the design. Every multiple is relative to the ORIGINAL ArchScale law η = 0.016 × (L/8)^−0.5 × (T/10.4B)^−0.32, computed from each run's actual peak LR (not from its Change ID's name), so it does not move if the ladder adopts a new law.

Notes

  • Models: the final checkpoints of Boxiang's ladder, re-evaluated by us (document-isolated: every document scored as its own sample).
  • overall_tw pools every split of val_v2, uncheatable, codefresh, v3small, private_internal and pile_test, token-weighted; overall_macro = mean of those six; pile_10k is reported apart. Units: nats/token.
  • CE = cross-entropy only; KD = (1 − α)·CE + α·KL(teacher top-64 + tail ‖ student), teacher MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL. KD's CE reference is the MuonH model of the same recipe (same data order and layout, α = 0).
  • Checked: every suite except private_internal matches Boxiang's doc-isolated results (≤ 0.00005).
  • Full per-model results (incl. 115 splits): trichord/dense_pretrain_result/<Change ID>_<rung>.json.
  • From Boxiang's results/<Change ID>/scores.json: the packed final validation of each training run (documents concatenated, no attention mask); we do not re-measure it.
  • Only his 6 pooled sets (val_v2 not split, no private_internal); “mean of 6” = the simple mean of those 6 (his definition).
  • Packed is ~0.013–0.016 above doc-isolated: do not compare absolute values across the two tabs, only deltas within a tab.

KD loss variants compared: same α 0.8, same MuonH

The 8 runs differ only in how the teacher distribution is truncated in the KD term: α = 0.8, MuonH optimizer, seed 1 and data order are identical; the baseline is still CE (MuonH, α = 0); B64 (top-64 + the rest of the tail as one bucket) is KD α 0.8 itself and is drawn as a line too, so each variant can be read against it. Negative = better than CE.

Naming: letters = tail treatment · number = top-k size · trailing Y = y computed exactly
PartMeaning
BBucket: the tail outside the top-k is merged into one outcome; only the student's total tail mass has to match
SSampled: the tail is estimated from the 4 tokens pre-sampled in the cache (unbiased)
DDData Draw: instead of the teacher's tail, the corpus's actual next token approximates it
DROPTail dropped: the teacher is renormalised over the top-k only (control)
64 / 128how many top-k tokens are computed exactly
Yy exact: when the actual next token y falls outside the top-k, y is taken out of the tail and computed exactly
